result.title: What Does Matching a Human Intervention Effect Establish? Benchmark Checks for LLM Simulations
result.summary: LLM simulations are validated by equivalence with human effects, yet a zero reference passes whenever the human 90 percent interval lies inside the margin, as the human benchmark shows before simulation. When the zero reference fails, planned precision gives independent simulations the margin up to which passing is a 5 percent test of response. In an exploratory 70-experiment reanalysis, 72 percent of GPT-4's $\pm$0.20 SD passes were zero-reference passes; GPT-4 passed 16 contrasts the zero reference failed (1.58 expected without response). In a preregistered audit, Claude Sonnet 5.5 passed three intention targets, all zero-reference passes, and the registered belief-gradient control; norm beliefs changed 0.065 SD against humans' 0.351 (zero-reference check added after unblinding; norm beliefs emphasized after inspection). Registered tests detected no overestimation; average-effect intervals excluded overestimation above 0.08 SD. A group audit's precision floor is 1.33 facts against a 2.9-fact effect. Report the zero-reference threshold beside every equivalence decision.

AI.brief_summary: 论文讨论如何判定 LLM 模拟“匹配人类干预效应”，指出等价性检验中零参照阈值会让空效应自动通过，并用 70 项实验再分析与预注册审计核查 GPT-4、Claude 的通过是否属于零参照通过。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“先给出零参照阈值再宣称效应成立”的检验逻辑可能可供核查 LVR 评价：模型在缺乏视觉证据或有效 latent 内容时同样越过阈值的情形，与该文的零参照通过同构，可用于设计“是否真正使用证据”的对照判定。
